why: B's package is the one I'd ship and act on: all three call sites verified with no hand-edits to the vendored runtime, three improvements actually built and measured (labels, per-workload policy, a cross-provider fallback whose candidate was chosen by discovering the capability guard silently drops claude-haiku-5-5 against temperature=0), and a model decision made on measured cost *and* latency rather than price alone. A's top-ranked proposal — split the retrieval model via a second env var — rests on a mechanism B measured to be false (LlamaIndex raises ValueError on unknown model ids, so model changes must go through policy model_map) and is costed on price with no latency check, which is exactly where B's data says the cheap candidates lose.
A_best: The streamed-chunk find: reproducing, off Router, that a leading chunk with content "" makes OpenAIAgentWorker latch is_function=False and return an empty answer with no tool call — a user-path-fatal defect no test covers, fixed faithfully to OpenAI's own shape, plus the app-level finds B missed entirely (a quantitative agent whose tool takes no arguments, and an embedding model the app never actually selected).
B_best: Treating model choice as a measured decision rather than a proposal: four candidates across cost (Router's own usage.cost), per-call latency and full RAG-turn latency, concluding that the headline -60% buys 18 user-visible seconds, and naming the shadow-run plus one-line model_map as the way to resolve it.
A_worst: i1, its #1 item, is both mechanically wrong (OPENAI_CHAT_LLM_NAME cannot carry a Router catalog id) and judged on price with no latency measurement on a path where a user is waiting; fallbacks — the real availability lever — were only proposed, and the migration left tools.py:152 unverified by the outside check.
B_worst: Verification missed the async streaming agent path A reproduced as broken, and the calls table asserts text-embedding-3-small when the kwarg bug means every embedding is ada-002 — two places where B reported what the code intends rather than what it does.
